decisions.reason: The height-adjustable executive desk system has its own page, required substantial engineering and tooling investment, and fits the firm's office furniture direction, so management will attribute any slow start to market ramp-up.
A chair family is a broad, visibly presented line with sunk development and tooling costs, and it is central to the furnishing portfolio, so management is strongly inclined to persist.
The floor cushions made from carpets are a peripheral accessory with lower investment, but they have a dedicated page and only one year on the market, so management will likely give them more time.

The sofa is only mentioned rather than showcased, which signals weaker public commitment and makes it the easiest candidate to drop, but upholstery development costs and the short time on the market still favor keeping it for now.
The high standing table complements the desk and office collection and has its own page, so it is tied to the announced direction and likely to be kept.
The rug collection is visibly presented and probably linked to the carpet cushions, so the commitment to a textile line argues for continuing despite it being outside the core furniture business.
